chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Bureyd ibn, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) recited: 'Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority from among you; then if you fear a dispute in the matter, refer it to Allah and to the Messenger and to those in authority from among you.'
Then he said: 'How can He command obedience to them and permit dispute with them? He only said that to the commanded ones, to whom it was said: Obey Allah and obey the Messenger.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia interpretation of 'those in authority' in Surah An-Nisa verse 59?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Abu Ja'far (Imam Muhammad al-Baqir) offers a nuanced exegesis of the 'Verse of Obedience' (4:59), addressing the apparent paradox between commanding obedience to 'Ulil-Amr' and permitting dispute resolution among them. He clarifies that the imperative to obey is directed at the general populace ('al-ma'murin') who receive the command, distinguishing their duty of compliance from the authorities' capacity for internal deliberation or dispute. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the hierarchical structure of religious authority and the specific obligations of the lay community.
